source_caption:
𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐁𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐞𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐈𝐧𝐢𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐧, 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟐.⁣
⁣
This movie is an idiosyncratic blend of funny, sad, and more than anything lonely, carried by one of the strongest casts of the recent years.⁣
⁣
Colin Farrell and Brendan Gleeson are both excellent, but the two standout performances for me were Kerry Condon as Siobhán and Barry Keoghan as Dominic. Both characters are deeply affected by loneliness and the fear of rejection. Dominic is trapped on Inisherin with an abusive father and has no real way of escaping his situation. He spends the film searching for connection, but when Siobhán rejects him, he loses what little hope he had left for a different life. Siobhán faces a different kind of loneliness. She is intelligent and curious, but feels trapped by the island and by her responsibility toward her brother. She dreams of something more, yet struggles to leave behind the life she knows. What makes these characters so compelling is how believable they feel. Dominic pushes people away through his awkward behavior, while Siobhán keeps people at a distance because she fears being trapped. Their struggles are different, but they come from the same desire: to find meaning and connection.⁣
⁣
There is so much depth to each character in this movie without overwhelming the viewer. That’s a rare thing. One of those movies that gets better with every viewing. A real gem. 💎

source_details.title: The Banshees of Inisherin
source_details.synopsis: The Banshees of Inisherin ( in-ih-SHERR-in) is a 2022 black tragicomedy film directed, written, and co-produced by Martin McDonagh. Set on a fictional remote island off the west coast of Ireland in 1923, the film stars Colin Farrell and Brendan Gleeson as two lifelong friends who find themselves at an impasse when one abruptly ends their friendship, with severe consequences for both of them. Kerry Condon and Barry Keoghan co-star. It reunites Farrell and Gleeson after McDonagh's directorial debut In Bruges (2008). The film had its world premiere on 5 September 2022 at the 79th Venice International Film Festival, where Farrell won the Volpi Cup for Best Actor and McDonagh won Best Screenplay.
